title: Deployment Properties Mixed with Application Wiring
damaged_code:
```yaml
# Spring/wiring configuration mixing object associations with credentials
beans:
  - id: databaseConnection
    class: com.system.infra.DbConnection # Changing this breaks class-loading invariants
    properties:
      - host: "10.0.0.12"
      - password: "production_clear_password" # Operators must edit this file live to rotate keys
  - id: billingService
    class: com.system.domain.BillingService
    properties:
      - database: { ref: databaseConnection } # Code assembly / wiring
```
pattern: One configuration surface combines structural component assembly (dependency injection beans, class bindings, object references) with mutable deployment properties such as credentials, hosts, or tokens.
why_bad: Forces operators to edit large, volatile structure files containing complex application internals just to update a password or hostname. Routine configuration changes expose structural wiring to accidental edits; a typo in the code-assembly section breaks core object references and turns an operational change into an opaque runtime crash.
detection: Configuration files or schemas where class names, classpath entries, object graphs, serialization mappings, or bean references appear alongside environment-specific secrets (passwords, tokens) and connection settings (hostnames, IP addresses) that operators must change independently.
counterexample:
Simple metadata manifest descriptors without this mixed editing responsibility; separate deployment properties injected into stable wiring.
```yaml
# application_secrets.yaml - isolated and strictly access-controlled
database_password: "highly_secret_password"
```
fix:
Keep component wiring in a separate code/configuration surface and inject deployment properties (secrets, hostnames) through dedicated properties files, environment variables, or secret inputs.
```yaml
# separate file: credentials.env
DB_PASSWORD="production_clear_password"
```
source: [Pragmatic Programmers] Michael T. Nygard - *Release It!_ Design and Deploy Production-Ready Software* (2007, Pragmatic Bookshelf).pdf, Section 14.2.; Michael T. Nygard, *Release It!* (2007), Chapter 14.2, "Configuration Files", p. 598-599.
